item.title: The road to Solwezi: a prison bus, a police escort, and a plea waiting at the end of the highway
item.description: Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu spent Sunday on the North-Western highway under prison and police escort, bound for the Solwezi Magistrates' Court, where they are due to take a formal plea this morning — and where the State must finally say whether it is ready to try the seditious-practices case. The treason case, the graver one, still has no courtroom at all.

item.title: 'Immediate effect', and no reason given: the President removes his deputy police chief — a day after her discipline tour
item.description: State House announced on Sunday that Charity Munganga's appointment as Deputy Inspector General of Police (Administration) is terminated under Article 270 of the Constitution. On Saturday she was in Northern Province telling officers the badge is public trust. No reason was given — and the rumours of a wider command shake-up remain just that.

item.title: The region's bishops close ranks around Alick Banda: due process, a fair hearing — and a pointed question from Lusaka about public interest
item.description: The Catholic bishops of Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe have issued a joint communiqué over the arrest of the Archbishop of Lusaka, calling for a fair, transparent and lawful process — days after the continent's bishops' symposium did the same. At home, the Movement for Economic Emancipation asks what public interest the prosecution serves.

item.title: How long may the State hold a treason suspect? Lubinda asks the question aloud — and the DPP reaches back to Shamwana for an answer
item.description: Given Lubinda has returned to the public argument asking how long treason suspects can be kept from a courtroom. The Law Association of Zambia has called for the release of detainees not brought before a court. The Director of Public Prosecutions answers that due diligence takes time — and cites the longest treason trial in the country's memory.

item.title: The Atlantic comes to the InterContinental: Hichilema opens the Lobito 'engine room' today — with the World Bank's operations chief at the table
item.description: Zambia and the World Bank host the Second Lobito Corridor Coordination Meeting today and tomorrow in Lusaka, bringing Angola, the Democratic Republic of Congo, development partners and private capital into one room. The ambition: a working economic ecosystem from the Copperbelt to the Atlantic — not just a railway.

item.title: Five million guests by 2031: the Vice-President's funfair speech puts a number on culture — and treats it as an engine, not a sideshow
item.description: Mutale Nalumango has reaffirmed the five-million-tourist target at the sixth Diplomatic Funfair in Lusaka, framing cultural tourism as economic strategy. The arithmetic behind the ambition: 2.3 million arrivals last year, a two-and-a-half-million target for this one, and a billion dollars in receipts by 2031.

item.title: 304 cases, 11 funerals, seven districts: the cholera outbreak is now official — and Lusaka's swept pavements are its front line
item.description: The Ministry of Health declared a new cholera outbreak on 30 September, with 304 suspected cases — 62 laboratory-confirmed — and 11 deaths across seven districts in five provinces as of 29 September. Chibombo carries the heaviest count; Lusaka District's 130 cases explain why Operation Clear Path emptied the CBD's stalls this weekend.

item.title: Sixty seconds to shake the champions: Blades beat Power with a first-minute goal and a cruel late own goal — and the Transition League has its storyline
item.description: Konkola Blades scored the season's first goal inside sixty seconds and beat champions Power Dynamos 2-1 in Chililabombwe, with Wilson Chisala's late own goal settling it after Amine Hiver's equaliser. Zanaco won at Nchanga Rangers, Nkana won at promoted Trident — the short season is already loud.

item.title: Two teams, two airports, one week: the Copper Queens fly at Uganda's Olympic gate while the futsal men measure themselves against Egypt
item.description: The Copper Queens have jetted out to Kampala for Thursday's Olympic qualifier against Uganda, chasing a third consecutive Games with an all-local interim bench. In Cairo, Andrea Cristoforetti's futsal side plays the first of two friendlies against Egypt, eight days before the AFCON in Morocco.

item.title: 'We did not find any head': the Chivayo family confirms the unthinkable — Thursday's burial at Glen Forest will go ahead without them
item.description: Wicknell Chivayo and Lucy Muteke will be buried side by side on Thursday at Harare's Glen Forest Cemetery — without their heads, the family has confirmed, and without body viewing. The funeral will be public; the DNA process continues; the region that watched the crash now watches the farewell.

item.title: Unopposed at the top, a ballot for the second chair: Mutti keeps the gavel, Chisangano beside her — and Mufumbwe's independent takes the third seat
item.description: The Fourteenth Assembly completed its only item of business on Friday: Dr Nelly Mutti was re-elected Speaker unopposed, Attractor Malungo Chisangano returned as First Deputy Speaker unopposed, and Mufumbwe MP Nshamba Muzungu beat Chipangali's Vincent Mwale by 166 votes to 58 for Second Deputy Speaker. Hours later the President received the trio at State House — and set them a legislative task.

item.title: 'It is well with my soul': the man who built the Tonse Alliance walks out of it — while its leader sits in custody
item.description: Dr Chris Zumani Zimba founded the Tonse Alliance, engineered its January congress and put Brian Mundubile on its ballot. On Friday he resigned in a first-person note — leaving a coalition whose president is in a maximum-security cell and whose factions he accuses of rehearsing an old betrayal.

item.title: A pastoral letter, a State House rebuttal: the bishops warn of crisis, the presidency prefers dialogue — and the detainees wait in Kabwe
item.description: The Zambia Conference of Catholic Bishops closed September with a pastoral letter raising alleged arbitrary arrests and questioning the management of the 2026 election. State House has rejected what it calls a crisis portrayal; the Tonse-Pamodzi Alliance has rallied to the bishops; and the churches' central demand — humane treatment, named charges, a competent court — now has a date in the High Court.

item.title: October 26 to November 6: three High Court judges will hear the detention petition — 42 days after the cell door closed
item.description: The constitutional challenge by Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 other detainees finally has a courtroom and a calendar. The petition asks whether arrests, transfers and restrictions at Mukobeko breached Articles 1, 13, 15 and 18 of the Constitution — and it is not, the courts desk notes, the treason case itself.

item.title: K20,000 bail and a weekly report to police: Tonse-Pamodzi's secretary general denies forging a businessman's signature over ZRIMS Farm shares
item.description: Celestine Mukandila, lawyer and alliance secretary general, has pleaded not guilty to two counts of forgery and two of uttering false documents over the surrender of shares in ZRIMS Farm Limited. The State called him a flight risk; the court set bail — and a trial later this month.

item.title: Operation Clear Path: the CBD wakes to a Saturday without its stalls — a city trades its pavements for a cholera fight
item.description: From this morning, Lusaka City Council and the Zambia Police are removing street vendors and unauthorised bus stops from the capital's centre. The mayor says it is order, not punishment; the outbreak numbers say why the city chose this weekend.

item.title: Tear up the monthly calendar: the President wants fuel priced in seasons, not weeks — and ADNOC wants to be in the room
item.description: Forty-eight hours into the K31.46 era, the argument has moved from the pump to the mechanism. President Hichilema told ADNOC's trading chief in Abu Dhabi that monthly price changes are no longer working; Lusaka is now weighing two- and three-month pricing windows, with VAT's December return hanging over all of it.

item.title: The empty half of the basket: Zambia's student-loans board takes a 45-per-cent funding gap to the capital markets
item.description: Nearly half of student-financing need went unfunded last year. Now the Higher Education Loans and Scholarships Board is asking banks, pension funds and insurers to buy into the business of sending Zambia to university — carefully, and with no bond on the table yet.

item.title: The Transition League kicks off today — champions Power open at Konkola, while Hamburg wires home word of Daka's torn thigh
item.description: The Transition League begins this afternoon with a single national kick-off time, champions Power Dynamos opening their defence away to Konkola Blades. The week's other football news is less welcome: Hamburger SV has confirmed a torn muscle fibre in Patson Daka's left thigh, suffered on Chipolopolo duty.

item.title: Derulo at dusk: the Stanbic Music Festival takes the Polo Field tonight — with its best circle already sold out
item.description: Jason Derulo headlines the Stanbic Music Festival at the Lusaka Showgrounds this evening, on a bill with Yo Maps, Mampi, Danny Kaya and Zimbabwe's Tamy Moyo. Gates at Polo Field A run from 12:30 to 23:30 — and the premium EN Circle is gone.

item.title: The Clerk, the gavel and 266 seats: the Fourteenth Assembly sits for the first time today — and can do nothing until it has a Speaker
item.description: The Order Paper for Friday carries a single line of business: the election of the Speaker and two deputies. Until that is done, the expanded National Assembly — 226 constituency seats and 40 proportional-representation seats created by the 2025 amendments — cannot transact anything at all. The President opens the session next Friday.

item.title: Home to the K31.46 morning: Hichilema lands from Abu Dhabi with US$2.14 billion in commitments — and says more is being finalised
item.description: The President returned to Kenneth Kaunda International Airport on Thursday evening quoting a figure of more than US$2.1 billion from his Abu Dhabi working visit — health, agriculture, tourism and energy, with a 100-hectare health city among the plans — while the forum's own count of signed instruments ran higher still. He arrived to the first full day of the new fuel prices.

item.title: Six aboard, no survivors: the Marondera helicopter crash that killed Wicknell Chivayo — and the DNA wait now holding the region's attention
item.description: Zimbabwe police confirm six people were aboard the helicopter that went down at Kudenga Farm near Marondera on Wednesday evening; the civil aviation authority's preliminary account says the tail struck first. Identification of the victims awaits DNA analysis. Tributes have come from Presidents Mnangagwa and Ruto — and the story has been followed as closely in Lusaka as in Harare.

item.title: Solar rows and a copper shaft: Britain's Africa trade commissioner ends a five-day Zambia pitch today
item.description: Alastair Long's Zambia programme closes on Friday after a week that took the UK Trade Commissioner for Africa from a GreenCo solar site to First Quantum's Trident mine — with the Green Growth Compact and British International Investment's strategy doing the framing, and a Terzeon reception doing the networking.

item.title: K3.3 billion in the furrows: on the eve of planting season, Indo Zambia Bank reveals the biggest farm book in its history
item.description: The bank's agriculture portfolio has reached K3.3 billion, it disclosed this week — K400 million of it through the smallholder facility that has reached more than 3,600 farmers — with earmarks behind it for soybeans, wheat and energy, timed to the season that starts with the first rains.

item.title: Day one at K31.46: the commuter arithmetic of a 24-per-cent jump, a kwacha at K19.61 — and December's VAT question
item.description: The first full day of the new pump prices dawned on the ranks and the filling stations with fares yet to move. But the arithmetic has moved: at long-distance consumption rates, the diesel line alone adds about K820 to a one-way Lusaka–Ndola run — and the VAT reinstatement dated for 1 December is still in the post.

item.title: 739 bags of suspected fake fertiliser, four men in custody: the DEC unearths an unregistered plant weeks before planting
item.description: The Drug Enforcement Commission has uncovered a manufacturing operation spanning 9 Miles and Meanwood Vorna Valley, seizing 739 bags of suspected counterfeit fertiliser, raw materials and equipment. An agricultural consultant and three businessmen face charges including money laundering — and the timing, at the gates of the planting season, is the point.

item.title: 304 cases, eleven dead, seven districts: Zambia declares a cholera outbreak weeks after the last one was declared over
item.description: Eight of the eleven deaths happened in the community — people reaching care too late. Acting Health Minister Gilbert Siame declared the outbreak on Wednesday: 304 cases across five provinces as of Tuesday, with Lusaka and Chibombo carrying the heaviest loads and a vaccination decision under assessment.

item.title: Ten matches, one kick-off: the Transition League begins tomorrow — champions Power Dynamos open at Konkola Blades
item.description: Every opening-round fixture kicks off at 15:00 on Saturday in a season built to move Zambian football's calendar: two streams drawn from last season's final standings, a new national cup alongside, and the champions beginning their defence in Chililabombwe.

item.title: Derulo at the Polo Field, thirty countries at the Showgrounds: a diary for a city in jacaranda season
item.description: Saturday belongs to the big stages: Jason Derulo headlines the Stanbic Music Festival from half past noon while the Diplomatic Fun Fair fills the Showgrounds. Beyond the weekend, October is stacked — theatre turns forty in Chingola, Barefeet turns twenty, and the virtual festival runs all month.

item.title: K31.46 at the pump: the tax holiday ends, excise returns — and Zambia wakes to its steepest fuel-price jump of the year
item.description: No statutory instrument appeared before midnight, so the six-month fuel-tax relief died on schedule. The Energy Regulation Board's October review restores excise duty and passes on dearer oil and a weaker kwacha: petrol up 24 per cent to K31.46, diesel up 24 to K33.27 — with VAT's return dated for 1 December.

item.title: “Instruments of justice and service, not sources of fear”: the Catholic bishops and the CCZ close ranks on the state of the nation
item.description: In separate but aligned statements on one Wednesday, Zambia's two largest church bodies questioned the credibility of the 2026 elections, decried arbitrary arrests and force that has cost civilian lives, and demanded an independent investigation into the killing of former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya. October, the bishops declared, will be a month of rosary prayers for peace.

item.title: “The outcome was never in doubt — the process is”: Antonio Mwanza gives the ECZ three questions, and a warning about 2031
item.description: The Democratic Progressive Party leader accepts that President Hichilema won — and says that is precisely why the Electoral Commission must now account for the suspended count, Mandevu's stolen ballots and a dead election agent. His prescription: commissioners chosen independently, a timetable that binds the incumbent, and public media that covers everyone.

item.title: Two hundred and fifty basis points: the Bank of Zambia delivers its biggest cut in more than a decade
item.description: Economists expected twenty-five. The Monetary Policy Committee delivered two hundred and fifty, taking the policy rate to 10.75 per cent — a fourth consecutive cut, powered by 6.1 per cent inflation, a record maize harvest and a firmer kwacha. The committee's own risk list, though, reads like next month's news.

item.title: K212 billion for creditors: the Green Paper prices the new term — and debt service outbids FISP, CDF and free education combined
item.description: The 2027–2029 Medium-Term Budget Plan, the Treasury's first blueprint of the new mandate, sets aside K212.2 billion for debt service — K63.6 billion more than the entire transfers budget for farmers, constituencies, pupils and school meals. The bill falls as a share of GDP only if the growth promises are true.

item.title: The Fund is back in town: Zambia opens successor-programme talks — and wants a deal before the year ends
item.description: An IMF mission led by Edward Gemayel is in Lusaka until 10 October, negotiating a successor to the US$1.7 billion programme that ended in January. The government is selling growth; the Fund is checking the sustainability file. Both are reading the same Green Paper.

item.title: “Not the Judiciary — the security services”: the State's answer for the three days the courts went dark
item.description: Attorney-General Mulilo Kabesha has told the Constitutional Court that August's closure of the courts was ordered by the defence and national security services, and merely communicated by the Judiciary. The admission — the first official attribution of responsibility — comes as the State asks that the Chapter One Foundation petition be dismissed with costs.

item.title: Five more carcasses in Nabwalya, twenty-six people on the register: the anthrax response races the river
item.description: Three more hippos and two more elephants have died of anthrax in the Nabwalya Game Management Area, taking the wildlife toll to 49 hippos, nine elephants and six buffaloes. Twenty-six human cases have now been reported — and investigators keep finding evidence that people are reaching the carcasses first.

item.title: 0.2 seconds at 18:21: ZESCO explains the night Levy Mwanawasa went dark — and promises new lights
item.description: The blackout that stopped Zambia's 2-0 win over Togo for eighteen minutes lasted, on the utility's account, a fifth of a second. The floodlights simply could not forgive it: their design demands about twenty minutes to return to full brightness. ZESCO will now engage the Ministry of Youth, Sport and Arts on a redesign.

item.title: Ten years of the Lusaka July — in October: “The Tale of a Ruby” opens at the National Museum on the 16th
item.description: The capital's most dressed-up weekend has a theme, a date and a tenth birthday. Lusaka July 2026 runs 16–18 October across three signature events, opening with a Night of Culture at the Lusaka National Museum — the social season's anchor, transplanted to the year's busiest cultural month.
